The test `testLoopingOptionLookAlike2` in the class `BugLoopingOptionLookAlikeTest` of the Apache Commons CLI2 library is failing. The test sets up a parser with two arguments - `inputfile_opt` and `outputfile_opt`, both created using the `ArgumentBuilder` with names "input" and "output" and with minimum and maximum values set to 1. The test then creates a `SourceDestArgument` using these two arguments and adds it to a group of options.

The failure occurs when the test tries to parse an array containing four instances of the string "testfile.txt". The test expects an `OptionException` to be thrown with the message "Unexpected testfile.txt while processing".

Based on the current bug report, there seems to be an issue related to argument defaults preventing command-line usage. The bug report mentions supplying a value on the command line intended to override a default value but encountering problems when the command line already has a value for this option.

Upon reviewing the code snippets related to the creation of arguments (`ArgumentBuilder`) and options in Apache Commons CLI2, there doesn't seem to be an explicit setting of default values for the arguments. This leads to a suspicion that the way default values are handled or overridden in command-line parsing might be causing the issue observed in the failing test.

To further diagnose this issue, we may need to investigate how defaults are handled in the command-line parsing process and whether overriding default values works as expected.

Shall we proceed with investigating the default value handling in the command-line parsing process?
